issues.title: Nested test delegate missing final modifier
issues.description: The rule requires that classes not designed for subclassing must be marked with the 'final' keyword to prevent unintended inheritance and enable compiler optimizations. The FakeWKNavigationDelegate class is a test utility not intended for inheritance but lacks the 'final' modifier.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

issues.title: Wrong frame captured in navigation delegate
issues.description: The delegate captures navigationAction.targetFrame instead of navigationAction.sourceFrame. The targetFrame represents the frame that will be navigated (which may be nil for new windows), while sourceFrame represents the frame that initiated the navigation. This causes the helper to capture nil or incorrect frame information, breaking all tests that depend on valid WKFrameInfo objects. The original intent was to capture the frame initiating the navigation request.

issues.title: Ignoring XCTWaiter result allows returning stale data on timeout
issues.description: The captureFrameAndOrigin method no longer checks if waiter == .completed before returning captured values. This means the function will return potentially nil or incomplete frame and origin data even when the expectation times out or is interrupted. The function may return cached/partial data from a failed navigation attempt, causing tests to use invalid WebKit objects and producing false test results.

issues.title: Test expectation fulfilled after wait causes timeout
issues.description: The expectation.fulfill() call was moved outside the decisionHandler closure and placed after the wait() call. This creates a logic error where the test waits for an expectation that will never be fulfilled by the decision handler. The expectation is only fulfilled after the wait times out, causing the test to always fail with a timeout error rather than validating the actual permission decision behavior.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31309 - Bugfix FXIOS-14456 #31308 ⁃ Fix test failing on XCode 26.2 to enable using this version on Bitrise

structured_output.summary:
This PR replaces the hand-rolled `MockWKFrameInfo` and `MockWKSecurityOrigin` test doubles with real `WKFrameInfo` and `WKSecurityOrigin` objects. A new `WebKitTestHelpers.captureFrameAndOrigin(for:)` loads a URL in a real `WKWebView` and captures the frame and origin from the navigation delegate's `decidePolicyFor` callback. The three media-capture tests in `WKUIHandlerTests` now use those objects. The motivation is sound: the old mocks subclassed WebKit classes and allocated them through a private `alloc` selector, which newer WebKit SDKs no longer tolerate. No remaining references to the deleted mocks exist in the repo.

The change has a real bug. In `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess`, the decision handler's `expectation.fulfill()` was removed, and the fulfill was moved to after `wait(for:)`. The wait therefore has nothing to satisfy it and will time out, so the test fails on every run. The helper also adds a network dependency on example.com with a 3-second window, which trades one flakiness source for another. Smaller issues are an unused `waiter` binding that will warn, and a comment that contradicts the code.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The PR fixes the real crash source, but it ships a test that cannot pass. `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` waits on an expectation that nothing fulfills before the wait returns, so CI goes red. The helper's network dependency and the unused binding are worth addressing in the same pass.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `WKUIHandlerTests` built fake `WKFrameInfo` and `WKSecurityOrigin` values through `MockWKFrameInfo` and `MockWKSecurityOrigin`. Both subclassed WebKit types, and the origin mock was allocated through a private `alloc` selector. WebKit's newer SDK requires real internal state, so these mocks now crash. The code under test, `WKUIHandler.webView(_:requestMediaCapturePermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:type:decisionHandler:)`, reads the frame and origin only to make a permission decision, so real objects are needed for the tests to exercise it.

The PR swaps those mocks for a `WebKitTestHelpers` utility. The utility loads a URL in a real `WKWebView`, uses a navigation delegate to capture `navigationAction.targetFrame` and its `securityOrigin` during `decidePolicyFor`, and returns them to the test. The three media-capture tests now call this helper first and pass the captured objects into the handler.
steps: Entry point: each media-capture test in `WKUIHandlerTests` calls `WebKitTestHelpers.captureFrameAndOrigin(for:)` before exercising the handler. This is the first place real WebKit objects are created.
Helper: `captureFrameAndOrigin` creates a `WKWebView(frame: .zero)`, attaches a `FakeWKNavigationDelegate`, and loads the URL. It then blocks on `XCTWaiter.wait` for up to 3 seconds.

Capture: the delegate's `decidePolicyFor` stores `targetFrame` and its `securityOrigin`, allows the navigation, and fulfills the expectation. The helper returns the pair if both were captured, or nil otherwise.

Handler under test: the test passes the captured `origin` and `frame` into `WKUIHandler.webView(_:requestMediaCapturePermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:...)`. The decision outcome is checked in the decision handler.
Defect: in `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` the decision handler no longer fulfills the expectation, and the test calls `wait(for:)` before calling `fulfill()` itself. That wait can only time out.

findings.title: testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess can never pass: its expectation is never fulfilled before wait
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/WKUIHandlerTests.swift`, `testRequestMediaCaptureSuccess` (around lines 43-55) never fulfills its expectation before `wait(for: [expectation])` runs. The decision handler only asserts `.prompt`, and `expectation.fulfill()` is called after the wait returns, so the test times out. Move `expectation.fulfill()` into the decision handler, as the sibling tests `testRequestMediaCaptureIsActiveFalse` and `testRequestMediaCaptureDelegateReturnsFalse` already do, and delete the trailing `expectation.fulfill()` after `wait(for:)`. Keep the decision assertion as-is.

findings.title: Helper makes the tests depend on live network and a 3-second window
findings.body:
`captureFrameAndOrigin` loads a real URL (the tests pass `https://example.com`) and waits at most 3 seconds for the navigation delegate to run. The PR description says this stabilizes the tests, but it adds a network dependency to a unit test target. On a slow or offline CI runner the wait expires, the helper returns nil, and the test fails with "Could not obtain WKFrameInfo", which looks like a WebKit problem rather than a network one.

The helper also calls `XCTWaiter.wait` and discards its result. A timeout is not distinguished from a real capture, so the failure message is misleading.

::code{file="BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/Utilities/WebKitTestHelpers.swift" lines="34-49"}

The delegate also calls `expect.fulfill()` on every `decidePolicyFor`. A redirect or a second navigation action would fulfill the same single-count expectation again, which XCTest reports as an error.

The frame can be captured without a network round trip. A `loadHTMLString(_:baseURL:)` call, or a data URL, still triggers `decidePolicyFor` with a real frame and origin. Alternatively, pass the origin's expectations into the helper and use `XCTWaiter.wait` only once, with a clear failure message on timeout.
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/Utilities/WebKitTestHelpers.swift`, `captureFrameAndOrigin(for:timeout:)` (lines 34-49) depends on a live network load of `https://example.com` and a 3-second wait. Remove the network dependency: load local HTML with `webView.loadHTMLString(_:baseURL:)` (or a data URL) so `decidePolicyFor` fires without network access. Also check the `XCTWaiter.wait` result and return nil or fail with a clear message on timeout instead of ignoring it. In `FakeWKNavigationDelegate.webView(_:decidePolicyFor:decisionHandler:)` (lines 20-29), fulfill the expectation only once, for example by guarding with a flag, so redirects cannot over-fulfill it. Update the three call sites in `WKUIHandlerTests.swift` if the signature changes.

findings.title: Unused `waiter` binding will produce a compiler warning
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/Utilities/WebKitTestHelpers.swift` around line 44, `let waiter = XCTWaiter.wait(for: [expect], timeout: timeout)` binds a result that is never used, which warns. Either remove the `let waiter =` binding and call the wait directly, or check the returned `XCTWaiter.Result` (for example, return nil when it is `.timedOut`) so the timeout is actually handled.

findings.title: Comment describes a hard-coded example.com load that the code does not do
findings.fixPrompt: In `BrowserKit/Tests/WebEngineTests/Utilities/WebKitTestHelpers.swift`, two comments do not match the code. The comment on line 41 says to use example.com, but the function loads the `url` parameter. The comment on lines 32-33 says it returns the "first valid" frame and origin, but `FakeWKNavigationDelegate` overwrites the captured values on each `decidePolicyFor` call, so it returns the last one. Fix the comments to describe the actual behavior, or make the delegate record only the first capture if first-capture is what the tests need.

findings.title: Replacing private-API mocks with real WebKit objects is the right fix
